title: Implied volatility, India VIX and reading the option chain
objectives: Explain implied volatility and the India VIX.
Read open interest and the put-call ratio without over-reading them.
body_md:
## Implied volatility (IV)

**IV** is the volatility that, put into the pricing model, gives today's market premium. Higher IV means **dearer options**; sellers collect more, buyers pay more. IV tends to rise before events and in falling markets.

## India VIX

A measure of **expected annualised volatility** of the Nifty over the next 30 days, computed from Nifty option prices.

- VIX of 15 means the market expects about 15% a year.
- Monthly one-standard-deviation move ≈ 15 ÷ √12 ≈ **4.3%**.
- High VIX: fear and expensive options. Low VIX: calm and cheap options.

## Reading the option chain

| Item | Reading |
|---|---|
| **Open interest (OI)** | Outstanding contracts per strike |
| **Change in OI** | New positions being added or closed |
| **Put-call ratio (PCR)** | Total put OI ÷ total call OI |
| **Max pain** | Strike where option buyers lose the most at expiry |

Heavy **call OI** at a strike is often treated as **resistance**; heavy **put OI** as **support**. These are heuristics: writers may be hedged or rolling.

## Good practice

- Compare IV with its **own history** before buying or selling options.
- Use the chain for context, not as a sole trade signal.

> **Exam tip:** VIX is a forward-looking, option-implied number, not past volatility.
example: VIX at 18 suggests a one-month Nifty move of about 18 ÷ 3.46 ≈ 5.2% in either direction at one standard deviation.
